This implies that hospitals may not always provide lower quality care on weekends due to lack of resources or funding constraints.

Furthermore, Prompt 3 indicates that having a regular primary care clinician can improve quality of preventive care for young children. However, this does not necessarily mean that hospitals provide better care on weekends. It's possible that the regular clinician may have more time and focus on weekend patients.

Overall, it seems that while hospital care is often impacted by weekends due to various factors such as lack of resources or staffing, providing lower quality care on weekends is not a guaranteed outcome for all hospitals. More research and targeted interventions may be needed to address these issues.
